items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Said I used to be -- we were just room buddies, I says. And he and his brother and I were very good friends.

ctx.x: Yeah, abandoned. And she was such a -- whatcha call this -- such a loving baby, you know, a loving child, you know. She had a way of impressing people you know. But in the story of the play, Curly McDimple, it was situated someone left this basket on this boarding house, you see. And they rang the bell. And the leading man, which is a great artist -- artistic tap dancer -- Don Emmons -- he was playing in it. And I think he and George Hillman were the choreographers of this Curly McDimple.

And George Hillman was playing Bill, you know. And they had -- when she sang she -- the landlord was coming around there giving this landlady a hard time about the rents or something, you know, paying the bills, paying the expenses, you see.
